spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** Autoregressive LLM inference has two opposite regimes: **Prefill** (processes prompt tokens in parallel via large GEMMs -> **compute-bound**) and **Decode** (generates 1 token per step -> **memory-bandwidth bound**).

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts HBM3 Bandwidth Bottleneck & Quantized Weight/KV-Cache Footprint (HBM3 (35 GB INT4) -> Tensor Core / Regs -> FP8 KV Cache -> Decode (~95 tok/s)); 3-Layer Calibration, Accuracy & Concurrency Benchmark Flow (Calibration Set -> AWQ / FP8 Pass -> Task Eval Gate -> vLLM Serving).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Match the quantization scheme to your GPU architecture and concurrency regime. An ML platform calibrates AWQ (`group_size=128`) on 256 production prompts, gates the checkpoint against BF16 on JSON-schema + GSM8K evals, sweeps batch=1..64 latency, and deploys.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Explore PagedAttention KV-cache management, speculative decoding, and continuous batching.

learningJourney.title: What is LLM Quantization (Prefill vs. Decode)

explanation.foundation: Autoregressive LLM inference has two opposite regimes: **Prefill** (processes prompt tokens in parallel via large GEMMs -> **compute-bound**) and **Decode** (generates 1 token per step -> **memory-bandwidth bound**).
explanation.core: A 70B model in FP16 consumes **140 GB** of weights—requiring 2x 80 GB H100s—and batch-1 decode on an H100 (3.35 TB/s HBM3) is capped near ~24 tok/s. Quantizing weights to **INT4 (W4A16)** shrinks weights to **~35 GB** (fitting on 1x GPU) and lifts the bandwidth ceiling near ~95 tok/s; **FP8 (W8A8)** uses Hopper Tensor Cores to accelerate *both* prefill and high-batch decode.
explanation.deepDive: In production deployments of LLM Quantization, GPTQ/AWQ & Inference Performance, watch how what is llm quantization (prefill vs. decode) interacts with tail latency, retry amplification, and partial failures. LLM quantization compresses 16-bit model weights and KV caches into 8-bit or 4-bit representations (FP8, AWQ, GPTQ, GGUF) to slash VRAM usage by 2-4x and accelerate memory-bandwidth-bound token generation.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Why Naive Rounding Fails (Activation Outliers)** as the intuition layer for LLM Quantization, GPTQ/AWQ & Inference Performance: The problem: see what breaks without Why Naive Rounding Fails under real concurrency or scale.
explanation.core: Transformer activations in models >6B parameters exhibit systematic **outlier features**: ~0.1%–1% of hidden channels reach magnitudes 10x–100x larger than the median. Naive Round-To-Nearest (RTN) stretches the quantization grid to fit one outlier, crushing normal weights into 1–2 bits and destroying reasoning and JSON tool calling.

Calibrate on 256 domain-representative samples (code, JSON, target languages), enable `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` for long contexts, and run task-specific evals (HumanEval, JSON schema adherence) + concurrency sweeps against BF16.

advanced.finalSummary: Because autoregressive LLM decode is memory-bandwidth bound at low batch sizes, moving from FP16 to INT4/FP8 cuts HBM reads per token by 2-4x while keeping accuracy loss under ~1% when activation outliers are protected.
advanced.summary: LLM quantization compresses 16-bit model weights and KV caches into 8-bit or 4-bit representations (FP8, AWQ, GPTQ, GGUF) to slash VRAM usage by 2-4x and accelerate memory-bandwidth-bound token generation.

prerequisites.title: Distributed & Application Caching
prerequisites.summary: Caching keeps a reusable copy of data so an application can avoid repeating a database query, calculation, or network call. It can make responses faster and reduce database load. The trade-off: the copy may be out of date.
